Looking for feedback on planning encounters and equipping the NPC's in an AD&D First Edition campaign.

I am having trouble planning encounters where the party has a challenge but is not completely overwhelmed or underwhelmed.

I want my NPC's to have a higher/longer survival rate without equipping them with magic items and powerful armor because I don't want the to deal with an uber powerful party when they win the battle and loot the corpses. The party currently has 9 characters (some people are playing multiple player characters). The party is made up of very experienced players who have standard responses to spells, weapons, monsters and encounters.

The party members can focus on one or two characters while the DM is playing everyone. The clerics, MU's, fighters, druids, monks, etc. It is pretty easy to plan for an encounter if you are only managing one or two characters. It is difficult to play every single character in an encounter and play each one intelligently. Sometimes they are simply cannon fodder to soak up the spells and slow down the fighters while you do damage to the party.

Unless I totally overpower my NPC's or outnumber the party they simply roll over an encounter with their skill, knowledge and experience. I am impressed every game with the solutions they come up with and how they work together.

So far my best strategy has been to separate the party members and/or flank them. They recognized my strategy and that they were being had. They are now quick to regroup, hold ranks, and execute an attack.

Hold on a tank works great but it gets old having the same attack from every hostile caster. Anti magic items/areas are good for slowing down a caster but again it is a strategy that cannot be used constantly. Environmental affects can be useful but a greased floor is just as dangerous to an NPC as it is to a player character.

I don't have any problem killing a player from time to time but I am more interested in a balanced enemy encounter.

How do other DM's balance NPC encounters with their players?

Any special tricks, items, strategies that you have found successful?
How To Match The NPC's Against The Pary

In my opinion tabletop RPG doesn't need to duplicate the constant fighting of melee. It sounds like you already have gold balance in your foe creation, and I take this question to really be 'how can I throw more shit at them without killing them?'

I have two solutions - start introducing NPC's who temporarily join them and then part ways. Build up these relationships between these NPC's and your PC's over time. Now when you want to test your PC's with some aggressive combat, put your NPC's into situations where they end up on the front line. Then you can balance the encounter with a buffer of error. If the die rolls don't go well for your NP character, it might be fatal, but then hopefully the PC's will understand and change to a defensive strategy.

The second idea is that instead of throwing more combat at them, do a lot more skill checks for plot devices and extra rewards. Players feel rewarded but don't lose characters if they fail.

I do have some recurring NPC's who have not had any combat with, yet. Currently they are in the Temple of Elemental Evil at the behest of several NPC's from Nulb. I introduced my own NPC's who are evil and the party has just figured this out (after being placed inside the ToEE)

I like your second idea. Definitely something I forget about. Thanks for your feedback.
